summary: No new trust boundaries. The brief writer routes through safe_factory_write_bytes, which rejects absolute paths and '..' parts, so a hostile task id in a tampered decomposition fails closed instead of escaping .factory/ (verified: the write returns False and the command exits nonzero). Verdict input is schema- and recorder-validated with closed vocabularies (three verdict values, exact key sets), so no free-form data reaches evidence unchecked. pr_ready's backstop treats the quality artifact as untrusted input — non-dict entries and duplicate verdicts fail the implemented check rather than passing. Brief content derives only from the recorded, gate-protected decomposition; no secrets, no network, no shell.
residual_risks: A tampered .factory/reviews/quality.json could claim implemented verdicts; unchanged trust model — evidence files are already integrity-covered by commit stamping and the frozen-gate audit, not by this change.
